scope: Shared operator-owned TLS certificate resolver and actual loopback TCP/TLS component tests; canonical runtime wiring compiles. Public HTTPS/proxy routing and the full native/WT/WSS reload cohort remain pending.
behavior: Load and validate the original bounded certificate/key files before canonical installation recovery/binding. Protocol-specific TLS config clones share one resolver.

Explicit trusted process-owner reload runs file work off executor. It serializes before reading, validates validity/chain/key match and retains every previously served DNS/IP identity before publishing one complete replacement under a short lock.

Identical certificate chain leaves revision unchanged. Changed valid identity increments revision. Invalid, expired, mismatched, oversized or narrower identity leaves the last valid resolver untouched. Handshakes perform no file IO/reload serialization.

New full TLS handshakes on an existing cloned listener present the replacement leaf under normal CA/name verification. An established encrypted session continues. After malformed key replacement, a third full handshake still presents the last valid leaf; all three sockets/server task join.
Envelope signing keys, configured client trust and application authority retain their separate enrollment and lifetimes.

verification.dependencies: Prepared existing234patch source-lock tree before build; no upstream edits.
